hints.title: Monotonic Order In-Place Pointer Transformation
hints.text: A BST visits nodes in sorted order when traversed in-order. Reassigning left and right references into prev and next constructs a doubly-linked ring.

hints.title: In-Order Traversal with Trailing Predecessor Pointer
hints.text: Traverse left child, visit current node, then traverse right child. Connect the predecessor node right pointer to current, and current left pointer to predecessor.

hints.title: Circular Linking Blueprint
hints.text: Maintain first and last pointers. In inorder: recurse left; if last exists connect last.right = curr and curr.left = last, else first = curr; update last = curr; recurse right. At completion, close circular ring by linking last.right = first and first.left = last.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: In-order traversal visits each node once with call stack depth bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting nodes into a separate array before re-linking uses O(N) extra space instead of in-place pointer reassignments.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place pointer rewrites operate directly on existing tree node objects.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct bidirectional circular linkage connecting first and last elements.
